content_html:
Social Media Manager Resume Example & Writing Guide (2026)

A social media manager resume has one job: prove you grow an audience that actually does something. Hiring managers do not hire for posts published or followers collected alone. They hire for the system behind the feed: the strategy you set, the calendar you kept, the community you answered, the paid campaigns you tuned, and the result that followed in engagement, traffic, or revenue.

This guide gives you an annotated example, a section-by-section breakdown, the bullet formula for social outcomes, and costly mistakes to avoid.

Quick answer: A social media manager resume should include a summary naming your platforms, audience size, and strongest outcome, a skills section with content strategy, community management, paid social, and analytics tools, experience bullets pairing each campaign with its result, and links to live accounts proving the work.

Key Takeaways

  • Every experience bullet follows the same formula: campaign + channel + outcome — what you ran, where it ran, and what it moved.
  • Lead with scope and the headline outcome: platforms owned, audience size, engagement rate, and revenue or pipeline tied to social.
  • Pair follower growth with a quality metric every time — engagement rate, saves, click-through, cost per acquisition, or attributed revenue.
  • Spell platforms and tools exactly as postings do — Instagram, TikTok, Meta Business Suite, Sprout Social — they are literal ATS keyword filters.
  • Link live proof: the accounts you grew, your best campaign posts, or a one-page portfolio with before-and-after metrics.

What Hiring Managers Actually Look For

Ask a head of marketing what separates a keep-forever social media manager from a risky one and it won’t be “great at social.” It’ll be:

  • Growth with quality attached. Followers gained while engagement held or rose — not growth bought with giveaways that hollowed out the audience.
  • A calendar that survives reality. Planned series, seasonal campaigns, and reactive posts shipped on time, week after week, not bursts followed by silence.
  • Community handled, not just posted to. Comments answered, complaints de-escalated, and regulars recognised, so the audience feels like a community, not a broadcast list.
  • Paid spend treated as a budget. Tests run, losers killed, winners scaled, and cost per acquisition reported honestly alongside the wins.
  • Reporting a non-marketer can follow. One page a month: what ran, what it cost, what it returned, and what changes next month.

Social Media Manager Resume Example (Annotated)

Below is an example for a social media manager in consumer goods. It’s fictional — names and companies are illustrative — but every bullet follows the pattern hiring managers respond to: campaign, channel, outcome.

LENA OKAFOR
Lagos, Nigeria · (234) 555-0148 · lena.okafor@email.com · linkedin.com/in/lenaokafor

SUMMARY
Social media manager with 6 years across Instagram, TikTok, and X, growing a skincare brand from 18,400 to 96,000 followers while lifting engagement from 1.8% to 4.6%. Own content strategy, community, and paid social end to end, with $240,000 annual paid spend returning 3.4x revenue. Known for series formats audiences return for, not one-off viral posts.

SKILLS
Content strategy & calendars · Short-form video · Copywriting · Community management · Paid social · Meta Business Suite · Sprout Social · Hootsuite · TikTok Ads · Google Analytics · UTM tracking · Creator coordination

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Social Media Manager — Verde Skincare, Lagos | 2022–Present

  • Own social for a skincare brand across Instagram, TikTok, and X: strategy, calendar, community, paid campaigns, and monthly reporting.
  • Grew combined followers from 18,400 to 96,000 in 26 months while lifting engagement from 1.8% to 4.6%, with saves up 3x on tutorial series.
  • Built a weekly tutorial series that now drives 42% of profile visits and 31% of social-attributed site traffic, published on schedule for 104 straight weeks.
  • Manage $240,000 annual paid social spend at 3.4x revenue return, cutting cost per acquisition 27% by killing underperforming audiences weekly.
  • Grew the email list by 12,400 subscribers from social lead magnets, with social-attributed email revenue of $86,000 in the last year.
  • Handled a product-quality complaint thread publicly, answering within 2 hours and publishing a fix timeline; sentiment recovered within 10 days with no paid suppression.

Social Media Coordinator — Northlight Agency, Lagos | 2019–2022

  • Ran day-to-day posting and community for 6 client accounts, from calendars and captions to comment moderation and monthly reports.
  • Grew a restaurant client's Instagram from 4,100 to 19,800 followers in 14 months, with weekend booking link clicks up 58%.
  • Coordinated 23 creator partnerships, tracking deliverables, usage rights, and performance against brief in a shared tracker.
  • Cut reporting time from 2 days to 3 hours per client by building a standard dashboard template in Sprout Social.

EDUCATION
BSc, Mass Communication — 2019

Section-by-Section Breakdown

Summary: platforms, audience, and headline proof in three lines

The example opens with platforms and scale, then the proof: 18,400 to 96,000 followers, engagement more than doubled, $240,000 paid spend at 3.4x return. Without a manager title yet, lead with coordinator scope: “ran posting and community for 6 client accounts, growing one from 4,100 to 19,800 followers with booking clicks up 58%.”

Skills: platforms and tools exactly as postings spell them

Social postings are keyword-dense, and applicant tracking systems screen for exact terms. Name your platforms (Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn) and your tools (Meta Business Suite, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Google Analytics).

Experience: every bullet pairs a campaign with an audience, engagement, or revenue outcome

The pattern is campaign + channel + result: “grew combined followers to 96,000 while engagement rose to 4.6%”; “cut cost per acquisition 27% by killing underperforming audiences weekly.” Scope matters too — 3 platforms, $240,000 spend, 104 straight weeks of publishing.

Proof: link the work, with permission, and never claim what you did not run

Link only accounts you ran, date your tenure beside each link, and describe agency work by client type when names are confidential. A resume that links an account it never touched fails the very test the role requires.

Social Media Manager Skills & ATS Keywords

Mirror the posting’s exact language and keep these groups on your resume:

  • Strategy: content strategy, content calendars, brand voice, campaign planning, editorial planning, audience research.
  • Publishing: short-form video, copywriting, Reels, TikTok, Stories, scheduling, Canva, CapCut, Adobe Express.
  • Community: community management, moderation, social listening, crisis response, UGC, creator coordination, influencer outreach.
  • Paid & analytics: paid social, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Meta Business Suite, Google Analytics, UTM tracking, A/B testing.

Check your resume against a free ATS scan — for example, Cvyon's ATS grader — before you apply. Social resumes fail most often on vague engagement claims and missing tool keywords, not on formatting. Start from a clean template gallery or resume builder option, then verify with the free ATS grader.

5 Mistakes That Cost Social Media Manager Interviews

  1. Vanity metrics with no quality attached. “Grew followers 400%” says nothing about engagement, traffic, or revenue. Every growth claim needs a quality metric beside it.
  2. Unquantified bullets. A bullet without a number reads as a guess. Followers gained, engagement lifted, cost per acquisition cut, revenue attributed — attach a number or leave the bullet out.
  3. Claiming accounts you never ran. Linking a famous account you merely posted to once destroys trust instantly. Date your tenure, name your scope, and link only what you owned.
  4. Creator-only framing. Videos made prove creator skill, not management. Pair output bullets with strategy, community, paid, and reporting work across channels and quarters.
  5. Unreadable formatting. Multi-column layouts, text boxes, and image-based PDFs scramble parsing, so your analytics section arrives as word soup. One column, standard headings, real text.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should be included in a social media manager resume?

A summary naming your platforms, audience size, and strongest outcome; a skills section with content strategy, community management, paid social, analytics, and tools such as Meta Business Suite, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and Google Analytics; experience bullets pairing each campaign with its audience, engagement, or revenue result; and links to live accounts or a portfolio proving the work, because social results are only believable when a hiring manager can see them.

How do I show social media results without relying on follower counts alone?

Pair every audience number with a quality metric: engagement rate, saves and shares, click-through rate, cost per acquisition, or revenue attributed to social. Follower growth alone can be bought or inherited, so pair it with quality proof: followers grown 18,400 to 96,000 while engagement rose from 1.8% to 4.6%, or paid spend returning 3.4x revenue. Name the platform, period, and starting point, or the number proves nothing.

What skills do employers want most on a social media manager resume?

Content strategy and calendars, short-form video and copywriting, community management and moderation, paid social campaigns with Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads, analytics and reporting with platform insights, Sprout Social or Hootsuite, and Google Analytics with UTM tracking, plus creator and influencer coordination. Postings also screen for judgement: brand voice under pressure, crisis response, and knowing which trend to skip.

Do I need a portfolio or links on a social media manager resume?

Yes, whenever the accounts are public and you have permission to share them. Link the two or three accounts you grew, your best campaign posts, or a one-page portfolio with before-and-after metrics and screenshots. A social media manager resume without a single live link asks the hiring manager to take every claim on trust, and most will not. Never link accounts you did not run, and never share private analytics without permission.

How is a social media manager resume different from a content creator resume?

A content creator resume proves output: videos made, posts published, and views earned. A social media manager resume proves the system behind the output: strategy, calendars, community, paid spend, and reporting, with outcomes across channels and quarters. Creator work belongs inside it, but it must sit beside audience growth, engagement quality, and revenue or pipeline results, or the resume reads as a creator portfolio, not a management record.

How do I make a social media manager resume ATS-friendly?

Keep it single-column with standard headings (Summary, Skills, Experience, Education) and real text, not an image of text. Spell platforms and tools exactly as postings do (Instagram, TikTok, Meta Business Suite, Sprout Social, Google Analytics), and save as a text-based PDF or DOCX. Run it through a free ATS grader before you apply — social resumes fail most often on vague engagement claims and missing tool keywords, not on formatting flair.
